name: 47187-sharegpt-8b-4gpu
hardware: 4x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 of ONE a3 node (--gres=gpu:4), sm90, NVLink between the four cards. Driver 570.195.03.
parallelism: TP=4, PP=1, DP=1 -- one vLLM engine, one node, four GPUs. Fixed: a run on fewer cards is a different setup.
architecture: Dense decoder, GraniteForCausalLM: 40 layers, hidden 4096, 32 query / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, bf16, ~8.4e9 parameters (~16.8 GB, ~4.2 GB per GPU at TP=4); the rest is in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), 8 streams held in flight, bounded at 500 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, warmup the first 20%, no cooldown.
workload: the 500-prompt ShareGPT draw in `configs/data/sharegpt-500-granite41-8b.jsonl`, materialised by `configs/data/make-dataset.py` (standard sampler at its default seed 0) and tokenised with the served checkpoint: 101809 prompt tokens and 108576 output tokens, prompts mean 203.6 (p50 76, p99 769, max 932), replies mean 217.2 (p50 172, p99 768, max 805). Raw completions (`request_format: plain`, no chat template) at temperature 0; the backend sets `ignore_eos` so each row generates exactly its own `output_tokens_count`.
purpose: An 8-billion-parameter chat assistant answering short conversational turns with eight concurrent sessions on a four-GPU node.
launch:
# The engine is a source checkout of 5ad11172b791 (`git describe --tags` =
# v0.23.1rc0-835-g5ad11172b791), a COMMIT and not a release; `configs/env.yaml: venv` names it.
model: ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b

# The generic path that adapts a Hugging Face model class to vLLM at load time.
model-impl: transformers

tensor-parallel-size: 4

# The request file's sampler caps prompt + reply at 2048, so this is its exact worst case; the
# checkpoint's own 131072 window would size a KV pool for a workload this setup does not run.
max-model-len: 2048

# The checkpoint's own torch_dtype, written out so a change of default cannot move the weight
# width between runs.
dtype: bfloat16

# NOT vLLM's 0.90 default, and the reason is arithmetic rather than tuning. Eight concurrent
# streams capped at `max-model-len` hold at most 8 x 2048 = 16384 tokens; at 40 layers x 2 (K,V)
# x 2 KV heads per rank (8 / TP=4) x 128 head_dim x 2 bytes that is 40 KiB per token per GPU, so
# 640 MiB of KV per card is the workload's ceiling. 0.35 reserves 27.7 GiB per card, of which
# ~4.2 GiB is weights, leaving a pool ~30x larger than the workload can ever fill -- exactly as
# non-binding as 0.90's ~100x, so no request is ever preempted or queued for blocks under either.
# What it buys: at 0.90 the engine demands 71.3 GiB free per card and refuses to start if anything
# at all is left on the node.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.35
